reviewed_by: Claude review of making the diagnostic log readers tolerate a torn line instead of logging one error per read
reason: recent_errors() recorded an ERROR for every line of errors.log* it could not parse, and that report is itself an error record appended to the aggregate it had just read, so one permanently corrupt line produced a new diagnostics.viewer_record_invalid on every read: 1168 of them on this machine's Core since a torn write on 2026-08-26, 59% of the current errors.log and 67 of the default 100-record viewer window, crowding real errors out of the diagnostics page. export() had the same per-line reporting. The record's copy was wrong as well, because reason_code_for() matches "decode" in JSONDecodeError and gave a stale log line the protocol_invalid family's text about a component returning an unsupported response and the operation not completing, when the read had returned every other record. Both readers now share _read_log_records(), which skips blank lines and lines that are not one JSON object, counts them per file, and reports them once per launch as integrity_failed with an honest cause and impact; the count is exposed as status()["unreadable_record_count"]. _append() writes through a completing os.write() loop instead of a buffered handle whose unwritten remainder is discarded when a later write raises (which is how the 2026-08-26 record lost its tail while its copy in sandbox.log stayed intact), and a write that fails partway terminates the torn line so the next record is not glued onto the fragment and lost with it. tests/v3/test_diagnostics.py adds three tests, all failing on origin/main: the reader test counts 4 reports for 2 reads before the fix and 1 after and asserts the records on both sides of the fragment plus the blank line are still returned, the short-write test asserts a 20-byte-at-a-time writer still lands the whole record and that the append retried rather than delegating to a buffer, and the failed-append test asserts the fragment owns its own line and the next record survives. tests/v3/test_diagnostics_api.py covers the status and errors endpoints that carry the new field. The native reader and writer get the same treatment, and diagnostics::tests::native_viewer_skips_unreadable_lines_and_reports_them_once_per_launch fails on origin/main with 2 reports for 2 reads; the three neighbouring native tests that exercise append() and the unwritable sink are selected with it.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/src file changes. ui/src/diagnostics/types.ts is untouched, and the UI never reads the new status field, so DiagnosticsPanel renders exactly what it rendered before. No screenshot baselines: nothing rendered changes. No Playwright: src/nebula/v3/diagnostics.py matches the catch-all core-api rule and ui/src-tauri/** matches desktop-shell, but the browser suites never create a corrupt log line, the diagnostics page reads the same errors and status payloads (one additive integer), and desktop-shell covers Tauri behaviour no browser test can reach. tests/v3/test_diagnostic_sensitive.py and test_diagnostic_guidance.py are excluded because the record schema, the sensitive-detail store and the remediation catalog are unchanged -- the new record supplies an existing reason family (integrity_failed) with per-call cause and impact overrides that guidance_for() already supported; both files were run locally and pass. The two compaction tests in tests/v3/test_orchestration.py remain red on origin/main for the reason recorded in earlier receipts and are unrelated to diagnostics.
